perspective:
From John Atcitty’s available perspective:

- He knows he is Alaska Native, a Heavy Equipment Operator, has a middle-school education, and teaches equipment operation at a community center.
- He knows Beverly Yan is his colleague at the community center, teaches adult education, and has a doctorate. He compares his own education to hers.
- During a joint class project, John set up equipment for a demonstration and told Beverly he hoped it met her expectations. He felt insecure about his educational background. He heard Beverly say she admired how he handles machines and that education isn’t just about degrees, but what you do with what you know.
- Beverly had praised his expertise in operating machinery. John thanked her, felt more confident, and suggested collaborating on a new workshop combining theory and practice. Beverly said she loved the idea, called his practical skills invaluable, and said they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, John worried he might not always meet the high standards they had recently set. He told Beverly this honestly. Beverly said she appreciated his honesty, suggested setting realistic goals, and said their combined efforts—not perfection—made projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, John told Beverly he was glad they talked and that being able to be open with her mattered to him. Beverly said she respected his openness, trusted his judgment completely, and wanted to keep the transparency going. John believed she valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner, which increased his sense of worth.
- Encouraged by their collaborations and Beverly’s expressed respect and trust, John felt ambitious and proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase what they had achieved together. Beverly called it a fantastic idea, said it was perfect for demonstrating the impact of their work, and wanted to start planning.
